title: Bone and Tooth Sampling for Collagen Extraction
author: Maciej T. Krajcarz
materials: Carefully remove the remaining dust with compressed air.

steps.title: Set up cutting workstation
steps.instruction: Place the cutting work station under a hood in a well‑ventilated, well‑illuminated area and follow all health‑security precautions.

steps.title: Cut bone or tooth fragment
steps.instruction: Using a rotary saw with a diamond‑coated blade mounted on an engine handle, cut a fragment of bone or tooth weighing between 0.12 g and 0.45 g; operate at low speed (<20 000 rpm), hold the specimen in one hand and the blade handle in the other, and exercise extreme caution to avoid injury.

steps.title: Weigh the sample
steps.instruction: Weigh the cut fragment on a laboratory balance (±0.01 mg) using a pre‑tared weighing paper or container, record the weight in the Bone sampling protocol form, and repeat sampling if the weight is outside the desired range.

steps.title: Clean or replace saw blade
steps.instruction: After each sampling, submerge the rotating blade in clean Milli‑Q water for several seconds; if any dust remains, replace the blade. Dry the blade by rotating it above the water for several seconds or by gently blasting with compressed air.

steps.title: Remove visible contaminants
steps.instruction: Mechanically remove all macroscopically visible soil, sediment, mineral precipitates, and non‑compact tissues (cancellous bone, dental cementum, enamel) using a lancet (scratching) or a rotary diamond‑ or corundum‑coated bit mounted on the engine handle, while preserving as much compact bone or dentine as possible and observing health‑security measures.

steps.title: Tidy cutting workstation
steps.instruction: Remove all dust from equipment, tools, work table and surrounding surfaces and disinfect all surfaces.

steps.title: Set up cleaning workstation
steps.instruction: Prepare a cleaning work station under a hood, well‑ventilated and well‑illuminated; avoid touching the sample with skin, cloth, or nitrile gloves and use only clean stainless‑steel or plastic (PP, PE) tools.

steps.title: Acetone ultrasonic cleaning
steps.instruction: Place the sample in a glass vial suitable for an ultrasonic cleaner, label with a waterproof marker protected by transparent scotch, add enough acetone to fully cover the sample, then place the vial in the ultrasonic cleaner filled with water up to the security level (not above the vial opening) and run for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Dispose acetone
steps.instruction: After the ultrasonic bath, carefully decant the acetone according to local chemical‑disposal regulations.

steps.title: Inspect and wash if needed
steps.instruction: If any dust or dirt remains visible in the vial, wash the sample with Milli‑Q water from a wash bottle over a sink (preferably over a beaker that can catch a dropped sample).

steps.title: Rinse sample and clean pliers
steps.instruction: Using clean pliers, remove the sample from the vial, rinse it with Milli‑Q water over the sink (again over a beaker), return it to the vial, and rinse the pliers with acetone.

steps.title: Repeat water ultrasonic baths
steps.instruction: Repeat the ultrasonic cleaning using Milli‑Q water (no acetone) at least three times or until the water is visually clear; use a low‑power ultrasonic cleaner (<600 W) or allow the cleaner to cool between cycles to prevent overheating and collagen degradation.

steps.title: Dry sample in oven
steps.instruction: Immediately after the final wash, place the sample in an open glass or ceramic container labeled with the ID and heat it in an oven at 40 °C for a minimum of 48 h.

steps.title: Clean workstation and tools
steps.instruction: Wash all tools (vials, blades, bits, lancets, pliers); reuse vials after removing scotch and ID label with acetone, rinse with tap water then several times with Milli‑Q water, and leave to dry. Remove water from the ultrasonic cleaner.

steps.title: Transfer to desiccator
steps.instruction: After the 48 h drying period, promptly move the container with the sample to a desiccator and let it sit for 30 min to equilibrate to room temperature.

steps.title: Store sample
steps.instruction: Place the sample in an ID‑labelled plastic zip bag or other plastic container (2‑ml Eppendorf vials recommended for small samples) and store it in a desiccator cabinet; under dry, cool conditions (≤ room temperature, humidity < 5 %) the sample can be kept for years before collagen extraction.

steps.title: Document remaining bone
steps.instruction: Return the remaining bone to its original container and add a note (on the container or attached label) indicating sample ID, analysis type, sample size, date, and operator’s name.
